title: A debrief with Ukraine’s soldiers
gist: Briefed by Ukrainian officers back from the front, a military historian reports that the front is now a 20km+ drone-policed kill zone with no real frontline, that AI's battlefield role is greatly overstated, and that US suspension of Starshield access is pushing Europe and Canada toward their own defence industries and satellite systems.

insights.claim: Ukrainian officers say there is no longer a frontline: dense unmanned systems and sensors let a few hundred defenders hold dozens of kilometres, forward edges are held lightly, and combat zones routinely run 20km deep or more, erasing the front-rear distinction.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Force structure and procurement should shift from mass manpower and armour to sensors, drones and precision fires.

insights.claim: About 85% of Russian human and equipment casualties are reportedly caused by UAVs or by artillery and mortars directed by them, and Ukraine routinely expends 9,000-10,000 UAVs per day.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Implies enormous consumable-drone demand; supports drone, sensor and counter-UAS supply chains.
insights.locator: The depth of these zones is covered by first-person view

insights.claim: Any NATO partner claiming to be drone-ready for the next war needs at least 3.5 million cutting-edge drones (a year's supply) and the capacity to replace them.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Sizing benchmark for European drone-manufacturing capacity and defence budgets.
insights.locator: Any NATO partner that boasts of being drone-ready

insights.claim: Drone development cycles fell from about seven months in 2022 to weeks now, with some tweaks fielded the same day, but Russia copies Ukrainian designs and counters each innovation, sometimes within a week.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Favours agile, software-like defence suppliers over slow legacy primes; Western procurement cycles look obsolete.
insights.locator: Development time for new kit, Artem said

insights.claim: Armour and UGVs remain vulnerable to drones despite cage 'turtles' and spike 'hedgehogs', so new scouting and escort drones now protect them; networks engineers and coders have become the most important figures troops report to.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Combined-arms now means drone escorts and electronic-warfare support; signals and software skills are central.
insights.locator: Regimental commander Andrey thought every soldier

themes.theme: AI hype versus reality at the front

insights.claim: A Ukrainian drone specialist says AI's contribution to the war is 'massively exaggerated', appearing perhaps one per cent of the time, mainly for navigating alternative routes for long-range strikes, with caution about using it to speed decision-making.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Discount defence-AI narratives; near-term value sits in drones, sensors and connectivity rather than autonomy.
insights.quote: AI’s contribution to our war is so far massively exaggerated
insights.locator: The debrief turned to President Trump's current obsession

insights.claim: Data centres are the latest escalation target, with Ukraine striking several Yandex data centres in retaliation for Russian attacks; the West has no coordinated, tested defence for such lightly defended targets.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Digital infrastructure is a conflict target; data-centre physical security and air-defence demand may rise.
insights.locator: Both sides' targeting of data centres is the latest escalation

insights.claim: Ukraine's access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink's more than 10,000-satellite network and the backbone of its communications, was throttled then suspended, disrupting missions and losing drones, with Musk saying the decision lies with Washington.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Single-vendor dependence is a strategic risk; allies will diversify satellite comms away from US providers.
insights.locator: Since then, President Trump has drifted further towards Moscow

insights.claim: There are currently six European commercial alternatives to Starlink/Starshield (two maritime-focused) with two more planned, plus ten in America, none yet fully developed, and a military satellite race and spread of Space Commands has begun.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Supports European and allied SATCOM and LEO constellation spending.
insights.locator: The good news is that there are currently six European commercial alternatives

insights.claim: The author argues Washington is pushing Ukraine and the wider West away from US defence industries; Europe and Canada are expanding domestic military manufacturing and procurement and will not return, possibly leaving the US facing a G3 with Moscow and Beijing.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Structural tailwind for European and Canadian defence industry at the expense of US export share.
insights.locator: In the final analysis, this amounts to Washington pushing Ukraine

insights.claim: After four and a half years, Ukrainian briefers view the war as Putin's and unpopular in Russia, believe the end will not be decided soon by Trump or anyone outside Russia, and hold that an announced ceasefire does not necessarily exist; Ukraine will fight on until Putin dies.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Do not price a near-term settlement; prolonged war supports sustained defence demand and sanctions regimes.
insights.locator: My briefers were unanimous in seeing the conflict as Putin's war

insights.claim: Russian forces remain poor because of recruitment from poorer regions, corruption and the lack of an NCO class, with top-down command crushing initiative, so Kremlin cost-benefit ratios are disastrous.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Russia's attritional capacity depends on manpower from poor regions; watch recruitment and fiscal strain.
insights.locator: In anything but a Putin-led dictatorship

insights.claim: Russian gains are often only cellars and tunnels, which a Ukrainian specialist likens to 'claiming control of an ocean from the seabed', so claimed territorial captures overstate real control.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Treat Russian territorial claims sceptically when assessing front-line trends.
insights.quote: That is not holding ground in a military sense. It is merely infecting it, temporarily.

insights.claim: Medical doctrine is changing: drones block medics and the 'golden hour' has gone, so every soldier must be capable of far more than basic first aid, with surgeons guiding procedures by video call and the bottleneck being getting blood and medications forward.
insights.speaker: Peter Caddick-Adams
insights.so_what: Implies demand for forward medical kit, blood logistics and telemedicine in future military procurement.
insights.locator: Zlata, a trained nurse, then revealed
